headline: Recommended a favorable report on an easement for a retaining wall at 3360 Whitney Avenue.
summary: A proposed easement for a retaining wall at 3360 Whitney Avenue, next to the Farmington Canal Trail, was recommended with 8 in favor and 2 abstaining. The easement was a condition of an earlier special permit. Members also approved prior minutes and canceled the next regular meeting.
decisions: Recommended a favorable report on the easement for 3360 Whitney Avenue, 8 in favor and 2 abstaining.
Approved the September 22, 2026, regular meeting minutes as written.

October 20, 2026 
The Planning and Zoning Commission, Town of Hamden, held a hybrid Regular Meeting on 
Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The meeting was held in-person in the Legislative Council Chambers at 
Hamden Memorial Town Hall, 2372 Whitney Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518, and remotely via Town 
Zoom teleconferencing at https://www.hamden.zoom.us/j/82468227728.  
 
Commissioners in Attendance: 
 
In Person: Michele Mastropetre (Chairman), Joseph McDonagh 
(Vice Chairman), Richard Pearce, Hannah Leckman, 
Barbara Andrews, Felicia Bond, Ronald Leonardo, 
Calvin DeMarsilis 
  Staff in Attendance: In Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Maisie Albis 
(Commission Clerk) 
Via Zoom: Tim Lee (Assistant Town Attorney) 
  
Chairman Mastropetre called the meeting to order at 7:01p.m. The clerk read the agenda into the 
record, and Commissioners and staff introduced themselves.  
 
A. Public Comment Session 
  Chairman Mastropetre called for comments from the public regarding topics within the purview 
of the Commission. There were no attendees, either online or in-person, and the Chairman closed the 
public comment session. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
B. Regular Meeting 
 1. C.G.S. §8-24 Review #26-452 
Proposed Easement for 3360 Whitney Avenue Associates, LLC  
Applicant: Town of Hamden 
Chairman Mastropetre requested that Mr. Livshits read his report regarding the referral. The 
report summarized the easement proposal, which would allow for the construction and 
maintenance of a retaining wall at 3360 Whitney Avenue abutting the Farmington Canal Trail. 
Obtaining the easement had been a condition of approval for Special Permit #25-1389. Mr. 
Livshits indicated that the proposal had been reviewed by the Farmington Canal Commission 
(FCC) as requested by the condition, as well as the Town Engineer and the Town Tree Warden. 
His report concluded with the recommendation that the Commission issue a favorable report to 
the Legislative Council.
Page 2 of 3 Planning and Zoning Commission 10.13.26 Minutes 
 
Chairman Mastropetre called for questions. Commissioner McDonagh asked whether the 
FCC had taken a vote to approve the proposal. Mr. Livshits said that there had not been a vote, 
and explained that the only action required was for the Planning and Zoning Commission to issue 
a report to the Council. He confirmed to the Chairman that the proposal had been presented to the 
FCC in July.  
The Chairman then asked about the plans for the replacement of trees. Mr. Livshits said that 
had been addressed by the landscaping plan associated with the prior special permit approval.  
Commissioner Leonardo wondered whether it was within the Commission’s purview to 
consider how the work would be performed. Mr. Lee relayed concerns raised by Commissioner 
Leonardo and Commissioner DeMarsilis that the construction might impact the Farmington 
Canal Trail. Mr. Livshits again referred to the prior approval, which he said had addressed the 
proposed grading and limits of disturbance. He noted that the plans had been reviewed by the 
Town Engineer and that BL Companies would be on site to oversee the work.  
With no further questions, Chairman Mastropetre called for a motion. Commissioner 
McDonagh moved to issue a favorable report to the Legislative Council regarding C.G.S. 
§8-24 Review #26-452. Commissioner Bond seconded. Commissioners McDonagh, Bond, 
Pearce, Leckman, Andrews, and Leonardo voted in favor of the motion. Chairman 
Mastropetre and Commissioner DeMarsilis abstained. The motion carried with eight in 
favor and two abstaining, and the Commission issued a favorable report.  
 
 C. Old Business 
 
 
 
1. Review of September 22, 2026, Regular Meeting minutes 
 Chairman Mastropetre called for any necessary changes to the meeting minutes. 
Commissioner McDonagh moved to approve the minutes as written. Commissioner Pearce 
seconded and all members voted in favor. The September 22, 2026, minutes were approved 
as written. 
   
D. New Business 
 
 
 
 
      
 1. Commissioner Leckman: “Home in Hamden” Website 
 Chairman Mastropetre noted that Commissioner Leckman had requested to add an item for 
discussion regarding multi-family housing. Commissioner McDonagh moved to add the item 
to the agenda. Commissioner Leonardo seconded and all were in favor.  
Commissioner Leckman encouraged members to visit a webpage for the newsletter “Home in 
Hamden” at https://homeinhamden.substack.com. She explained that Issue 19 of the newsletter 
included a compilation of over 200 existing two- and three-family homes found in areas currently 
zoned for single-family housing. The authors of the newsletter advocate for changes to the zoning 
regulations that would allow for new construction of such homes in these zones, Commissioner 
Leckman reported. Mr. Livshits shared his screen to project the website for the Commission.
Page 3 of 3 Planning and Zoning Commission 10.13.26 Minutes 
 
2. Cancelation of Upcoming Meeting 
 Chairman Mastropetre noted that October 27, 2026, Regular Meeting would be canceled.   
 
3. Town Center Master Plan 
 Mr. Livshits informed the Commission of a webpage with information regarding the Hamden 
Town Center Master Plan. He shared his screen to display the page, which includes up-to-date 
project details, engagement opportunities, workshop recordings, and an ArcGIS story map. He 
encouraged members to visit the page for more information.  
Link: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/0f6a98a6ff694764a0bf687527e39584 
 
E. Adjournment  
 Chairman Mastropetre called for a motion to adjourn. Commissioner DeMarsilis made the 
motion, seconded by Commissioner Leckman. All were in favor and Chairman Mastropetre 
adjourned the meeting at 7:23 p.m.
